Cc: security@bellwetherhealth.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence playback & dataflow trace request (DPIA)

Marissa —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our DPIA update and the upcoming procurement review we need: 

- A time-limited, read-only "playback" of the relevant dataflows (pseudonymised sample) for the period 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-31 so our privacy team can validate the processing activities and minimisation controls.
- A snapshot of the current subprocessor chain (names, roles, countries, transfer mechanisms) plus evidence of contractual Art. 28 clauses and any SCCs or equivalent safeguards in place.
- An excerpt of access/audit logs for the playback period showing which service accounts accessed the dataset and any cross-border exports.

We understand there are security constraints; the playback can be done in a secure, screened environment (we can provide a list of approved reviewers). Please include expected timelines, any EDR/ops runbooks you require, and whether a formal DPA addendum or minimal licensing redline is needed before we can view the artifacts.

Claire
Claire O'Neil
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Bellwether Health

Claire —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can support a playback + trace package but want to align on three gates up front:

1) Scope confirmation: which product endpoints and dataset identifiers should be included (e.g., prod:account-bw-*/event-stream).
2) Reviewer access model: secure viewer list vs. time-limited SSO link.
3) Data treatment for the sample: full pseudonymisation vs. tokenised redaction — which do you prefer?

High-level plan and ETA:
- We can generate the subprocessor snapshot and Art.28/30 evidence summary within 3 business days.
- Playback environment + pseudonymised sample: target delivery 5 business days after scope confirmation.
- Access logs excerpt: 2 business days after playback is ready (we will redact identities of internal operator accounts where appropriate).

Jonas (Legal Ops) and Karthik (Privacy/Infra) are cc'd to confirm operational constraints. If you can confirm scope and reviewer list by Monday 24 Aug we can start on Tuesday.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Karthik —

Operational notes for the record and what we'll attach to the packet: 

- Subprocessor snapshot: we'll pull the canonical inventory (includes contract date, jurisdiction, data categories processed). Attached as CSV.
- Art. 28/30 evidence: summary doc that maps each processing activity to the Article 28 clause and the technical controls in place (KMS, VPC peering, tokenisation).
- Playback runbook: steps to create a pseudonymised sample, hashing rules, and the ephemeral environment config (IP allow-list, no-download viewer).
- Audit log excerpt: we'll provide JSONL with event timestamps, service account IDs (pseudonymised), and destination IPs — redaction marker for internal operator names.

Caveats: For cross-border transfer evidence we can show transfer mechanisms (SCCs, BCRs, or adequacy) but cannot export full raw logs that contain customer PII. If Bellwether requires additional attestation (e.g., on-prem inspection), flag that now so we can route to Sales Ops for a quote.

Attaching initial files and a proposed timeline.

Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Ops (Privacy)
Redwood Inference
